MGM Resorts Narrows Net Loss to $17 Million in Q3 as MGM China Grows 5%

Published November 2, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

MGM Resorts International reported $4.2 billion in revenue for the third quarter of 2026, down 1% year over year, and narrowed its net loss attributable to the company to $17 million from a $285 million loss in the same quarter last year. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $403 million, down from $506 million a year earlier. CEO Bill Hornbuckle said softer room rates weighed on the quarter but that trends had "rebounded favorably" in October.

Vegas and regional operations soften, Macau keeps growing

MGM's Las Vegas Strip resorts generated $2.0 billion in revenue, down 2% year over year, with segment adjusted EBITDAR falling 12% to $531 million from $601 million, which the company attributed largely to lower room rates. Regional operations outside Nevada brought in $883 million, down from $957 million, with segment EBITDAR down 18% to $243 million from $296 million. MGM China was the bright spot: revenue rose 5% to roughly $1.1 billion, though segment EBITDAR there still slipped 7% to $264 million from $284 million. Hornbuckle credited the China unit with "strong market-share performance" without citing a specific figure.

Digital units cited for "strong" growth, no numbers given

Hornbuckle said the company's digital businesses, including the BetMGM North America joint venture and MGM Digital, posted "strong topline growth" during the quarter, though the company did not break out specific revenue or EBITDA figures for either unit in the reported results.

Why it matters

The results land MGM in a now-familiar pattern among major Strip operators this earnings season: a softer domestic Las Vegas and regional picture offset by growth elsewhere, whether that's Macau's rebound for MGM or the digital and international businesses other operators have leaned on. For a company whose stock and narrative have both been shaped this year by takeover speculation, a narrower net loss and a CEO pointing to an October rebound give MGM a steadier footing heading into the holiday travel season, even as the quarter's headline revenue figure still slipped slightly from a year ago.
